title: The Rotavirus Vaccine Story: From Discovery to the Eventual Control of Rotavirus Disease.
ehr_evidence: The medical and public health communities were challenged to improve child survival through research by “taking science to where the problems were” [7].
summary: This manuscript details the discovery, development, and eventual control of rotavirus disease through the introduction of live oral vaccines, highlighting challenges and future directions.
key_findings: Worldwide, rotavirus is the leading pathogen causing severe diarrhea in children and a major cause of under 5 years mortality.
The first rotavirus vaccine, RotaShield, was withdrawn due to a rare adverse event (intussusception).
Newer vaccines (Rotarix and Rotateq) demonstrated efficacy in reducing rotavirus disease but showed lower effectiveness in low-income countries.
Two Indian-made rotavirus vaccines (Rotavac and Rotasiil) have been prequalified by the WHO and are being used in low-income countries.
Rotavirus vaccine programs have led to a marked decrease in hospitalizations and deaths from diarrhea.
population: Children under 5 years of age worldwide
limitations: The manuscript is a historical review and does not present new data.
data_availability_statement: Supplementary materials are available at The Journal of Infectious Diseases online.
